title: Three checks, one complete job
hook: Each checkpoint can miss a step. What survives three independent checks?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Compute serial completion from independently stipulated checkpoint reliability, and identify independence as the boundary.

misconception: A 5% miss rate at each of three checkpoints means only 5% can fail overall.
objective: Compute serial completion from independently stipulated checkpoint reliability, and identify independence as the boundary.

claims.text: Original stipulated compound model: A inputs [100, -10, 3, 0] yield 72.9; B inputs [100, -5, 3, 0] yield 85.7375. Prediction correct option 85.74. Retaining 90% at each checkpoint leaves {A}%; retaining 95% leaves {B}%. Each checkpoint multiplies what remains. Independent misses are stipulated; these are not measured checklist effects. Prediction explicitly asks the three-checkpoint 95%-retention case: 100 × 0.95³ = 85.7375%, displayed as 85.74%.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy parcel has two independent 80% completion checks. What percentage completes both? The retained share is 100 × 0.8 × 0.8 = 64%; adding the two pass rates is invalid.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, compound, inputs [100, -20, 2, 0], output 64; independent Python recomputation.
